context: Done with your tutorial?
Yes, finally finished.
message: Want to get dinner at the food court beside the station?

context: I am heading to the cafe downstairs.
I might get a drink too.
message: Do you feel like coffee or something cold?

context: Have you eaten anything today?
Only a sandwich this morning.
message: What kind of food are you in the mood for tonight?

context: We can grab supper after the film.
Sounds good, I know a place near the cinema.
message: Which supper place did you have in mind?

context: The canteen is packed right now.
We could try somewhere less crowded.
message: How about the noodle shop across the road instead?

context: I booked a clinic appointment for this afternoon.
What are you getting checked?
message: My eyelid has been bothering me, so I want the doctor to look at it.

context: I have an interview first thing tomorrow.
How are you feeling about it?
message: Quite nervous honestly, I keep worrying that I will blank out.

context: The presentation did not go as planned.
Oh no, what happened during it?
message: I forgot a section halfway through and felt so embarrassed.

context: I will be late because I missed my bus.
No problem, I am still at the cafe.
message: Thanks for waiting, today has been a bit of a mess.

context: I got the internship offer!
You were waiting for that email all week.
message: I am so relieved that they finally got back to me.

context: I have arrived at the sports hall.
I am walking over from the bus stop.
message: Should I wait by the ticket counter or go inside first?

context: Where should we meet before the concert?
I will wait at the entrance facing the river.
message: Which entrance are you waiting at again?

context: Is everyone ready for the group photo?
I am here, but Maya has not arrived yet.
message: Do you want to wait a few minutes for Maya?

context: I could not find the room for our discussion.
It is the small room beside the lift.
message: Ah found it, are you already inside?

context: I will get us a table near the window.
Message me when you enter the cafe.
message: I just walked in through the side door, where are you sitting?

context: I wrote a draft of the introduction.
I can help you look through it.
message: Could you check whether the second paragraph is too repetitive?

context: Our slides need to be uploaded before midnight.
I have already uploaded my section.
message: Please remember to upload your slides tonight.

context: Have you managed to start the practice questions?
I finished the first two but got stuck on the third.
message: Which question are you stuck on exactly?

context: The submission deadline has moved to next Monday.
That gives us more time to check the references.
message: Should we use tomorrow to go through the references together?

context: I missed the first half of the lecture.
I took notes from the beginning.
message: Could you tell me what the lecturer covered before I arrived?

context: What time can you reach the station tonight?
I cannot get there before half past seven.
message: Would meeting at seven sharp be okay for you?

context: Can we plan our project meeting this week?
I am busy all Tuesday, but Wednesday afternoon is free.
message: Shall we meet on Tuesday after lunch then?

context: Let us choose a place for dinner.
I need to keep dinner under fifteen dollars today.
message: Are you okay with the thirty-dollar set menu?

context: How long can you stay at the exhibition?
I need to leave by three to pick up my sister.
message: Could you stay until four and help pack up?

context: Would you like to join us for the weekend trip?
I cannot make it this weekend, but I am free the weekend after.
message: Can you come along this Saturday morning?

context: Thanks for lending me your portable fan.
No problem, you can use it during the event.
message: Can I return your fan tomorrow instead of this evening?

context: Did my spare umbrella help yesterday?
Yes, I still have your umbrella with me.
message: Could you bring my umbrella back when we meet tonight?

context: I think I left my notebook on your desk.
Yes, your notebook is beside my laptop.
message: Do you still have my notebook there?

context: I borrowed your HDMI adapter for class.
I will need my adapter for a presentation tomorrow.
message: Should I return your adapter before your presentation?

context: You can borrow my tote bag for the books.
Thanks, I will bring your tote bag home today.
message: Could you return my tote bag at our next study session?
